stem: Two genetically identical clones are grown under different environmental conditions and develop noticeably different plant structure. What is the best explanation?
choices: Phenotype can reflect both genotype and environment
The clones may still share the same genotype, but structural differences indicate that one clone accumulated a stable genetic change during growth
Environmental conditions can influence plant growth, but expressed structural traits are determined mainly by the inherited genotype once clones are established
Visible plant structure is a practical estimate of genotype, so different morphology usually means the two clones should be treated as genetically distinct
rationale: Genetically identical material can express different phenotypes when environmental conditions differ. Phenotype is an observed outcome influenced by genotype and environment.
